Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one native transparent raster animation frame for the existing Silent Hill Combat project.
Primary request: Silent Hill 1 (PlayStation, 1999) Air Screamer, one entire creature in a STRICT RIGHT-FACING LATERAL FLIGHT PROFILE, NEUTRAL/MID-STROKE wing pose, for frame 0 of a coherent 3-pose wingbeat. This is a visual reconstruction candidate, not a claimed exact game extraction.
Input roles: image 1 is the original SH1 frontal creature artwork, governing its leathery brown mottled material, long tapering head/beak, skeletal build, two membranous wings and two short hanging hind legs. Image 2 is original SH1 gameplay rear view, supporting the same identity, not its camera. Image 3 is the project's already-used lateral glide frame and is the PRIMARY CONTINUITY reference for the EXACT head/neck/torso/hind-leg shape, proportions, side, texture and wing planform. Reproduce the SAME creature as image 3, not a new interpretation.
Framing: landscape canvas approximately 1536 x 1024, transparent RGBA. Camera exactly level from the side; head and long pointed beak point horizontally RIGHT; body axis horizontal. One body, one head, two wings, two small bent dangling hind legs. Keep the entire head, beak tip, both wing tips and both feet within canvas with generous clear alpha margins. Place the torso/wing-root around x=55%, y=52%, beak tip around x=89%, y=54%, feet around y=68%, wing tips extending left near x=12%. Leave extra empty room above AND below for the later high and low wing poses.
Pose: keep image 3's lateral body/head/neck and both legs fixed, but bring the near wing down into a neutral midstroke position, both leathery wings extended back/left in a shallow nearly horizontal sweep, slightly separated only so both can be read. Do not adopt the original artwork's frontal symmetrical wingspan. Match image 3's skin markings, bony wing spars, pointed scalloped membrane edge, lean torso and long shallow curved beak. Do not add feathers, horns, teeth, eyes, tail spikes, fingers, an extra tail or additional limbs. Preserve ambiguous original anatomy rather than decorating it.
Medium/lighting: detailed native raster cutout, muted brown/ochre/gray flesh leather as image 3, stable gentle neutral lighting. No arena, floor, shadow, glow, checkerboard, border, text, labels, particles or contact sheet. Only ONE whole subject. True alpha transparency, no translucent haze outside the silhouette.

Exactly two wings and two legs; retain natural overlapping far-side wing, not a frontal symmetric wingspan. No new limb, feather, crest, horn, teeth, eye, tail or tail spike. Both wing tips and all body parts must remain fully inside the canvas with clear transparency around them. No environment, floor, shadow, glow, haze, text, checkerboard, sheet or duplicate figure. Preserve TRUE alpha transparency; the brown/black preview background around the original is invisible RGB beneath alpha zero, not something to paint. Output only ONE full creature cutout.
Target wing pose: UPSTROKE/HIGH WINGS. Raise BOTH membranous wings conspicuously above their fixed body roots, in a synchronized wingbeat, while they continue to sweep back toward the LEFT. The near wing should occupy the upper-left region and its leading spar rise above the torso, far wing slightly behind it. The wing tips must stay clear of the upper border, roughly y=15–22% of the same canvas. Keep the entire head/body/legs and beak absolutely in their neutral-frame positions. The only visual change should be the wings moving upward; do not make the torso bob or the head tilt.
